newsitem.title: UK: London gold slumbers, platinum probes $390 level.
newsitem.headline: London gold slumbers, platinum probes $390 level.

text.p: The soporific gold market on Wednesday shrugged off losses in the dollar and stocks sparked by news the U.S. trade deficit had soared to eight-year highs.
"All the precious metals are sleeping," a dealer said. "There is just no interest."
Bullion closed at $383.35 an ounce, just $0.20 lower from Tuesday's London finish.

Prices have been virtually paralysed in recent days in anticipation of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting later on Wednesday to discuss a proposal to sell gold reserves to help finance assistance to poor countries.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said he was uncertain whether the plan to sell about five million ounces of the IMF's 104 million ounce gold reserves would be agreed on Wednesday.
But a number of dealers and analysts said they doubted that a decision would produce much drama.
"It's already been discounted," a dealer said, adding that the volume of gold in question was too small to have a significant effect on the bullion market.
A modest rally was quite possible, however, dealers said.
"The funds are short, thinking the IMF sale is a done deal, even though it looks like it may go the other way," a dealer said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see a shortcovering rally."
Selling by gold miners was expected to apply downside pressure if prices rose to around $385.
But fresh demand from jewellery manufacturers, boosted by the approach of the Indian festival season, was keeping gold prices above the $382 support area.
Platinum showed sudden verve in the otherwise moribund precious metals complex when it rallied to the $390 resistance level. It ended $2.40 higher at $390.90 an ounce.
Dealers said brighter technical indicators were attracting a bit of buying. "It's looking quite positive on the charts, and if it closes on the highs it will look good for tomorrow," a dealer said.
Palladium gathered no strength from gains in its sister metal and continued to trade at three-year lows. It closed $0.60 easier at $121.15.
Silver finished two cents firmer at $5.09, and appeared firmly esconced within its recent $5.00-$5.15 range.
